hypotheses.justification: The theorem also takes `[T2Space X]` from the same `variable` line, and `[T2Space X]` is needed because `injG` takes it. Mathlib has `instance (priority := 100) T2Space.t1Space [T2Space X] : T1Space X` (Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Hausdorff.lean:115). So `[T1Space X]` is implied by the other hypotheses. The only place the statement uses T1Space is as an instance argument of `injG`, through `compOpens` in `injPatch`/`cleanNbhd`. Without the binder, that argument is filled in by `T2Space.t1Space`, so the statement elaborates and means the same thing. The proof is unchanged. It only unfolds `injG` as a `dite` and uses `dite_eq_right`, so it never touches the T1 instance. Deleting the argument, for example with `omit [T1Space X] in`, is therefore harmless. The other instances are needed: `injG` or `cleanNbhd` uses `CompactSpace` (`isCompact_univ`), `DecidableEq` (`Finset.erase`) and `IsManifold`. I did not check whether `T2Space` is also removable, and it can't be removed together with `T1Space`.
